Colour guides that show the scene's shading

Source: R/guides-colour.R
guide_colourbar_3d.Rd

guide_colourbar_3d() with along an axis draws a colourbar beside the selected box edge of that position guide. The axis supplies its ticks, labels and title. The colour aesthetic and that position must map the same expression in every layer using the colour scale. Scale transformations may differ: colours are evaluated at the position axis's original data values. With along = NULL it is an ordinary legend-box colourbar (ggplot2::guide_colourbar()).

Usage

guide_colourbar_3d(
  along = "z",
  width = grid::unit(2, "mm"),
  gap = grid::unit(0.5, "mm"),
  nbin = 128L,
  shading.range = FALSE,
  ...
)

guide_coloursteps_3d(..., shading.range = TRUE)

guide_legend_3d(..., lit = TRUE, normal = c(0, 0, 1), shading.range = FALSE)

guide_bins_3d(..., lit = TRUE, normal = c(0, 0, 1), shading.range = FALSE)

Arguments

along

Position axis beside which the bar is drawn, one of "x", "y", "z", or NULL for a legend-box colourbar.

width, gap

Physical grid units for the axis colourbar width and its gap from the edge. Tick lengths include this space.

nbin

Number of colour intervals along the bar.

shading.range

FALSE, TRUE, or two angles in degrees in [0, 180], the span of light shown.

...

Arguments passed to ggplot2::guide_colourbar(), ggplot2::guide_coloursteps(), ggplot2::guide_bins() or ggplot2::guide_legend().

lit

Whether shaded layers use lit facet keys.

normal

Finite nonzero model-space facet normal, length three.

Value

A ggplot2 guide.

Details

guide_coloursteps_3d() and guide_bins_3d() are ggplot2::guide_coloursteps() and ggplot2::guide_bins() with shading; guide_legend_3d() and guide_bins_3d() draw keys of shaded layers as a small facet lit by the plot's light and first camera. normal specifies the facet's model-space normal. Unshaded layers retain their own key geometry.

shading.range shows what the light does to each colour. The colourbars and colour steps become a two-dimensional swatch, value along the bar and light across it; legend and bin keys get a strip below the facet. The colours come from the same shading kernel as the faces, for a surface whose normal makes each angle along the range with every light, without the specular term, using the material of the first layer with one. TRUE spans 90 to 0 degrees for the "multiply" and "tint" modes of lights_3d() (from ambient to full light) and 180 to 0 degrees for the signed modes; two angles in degrees, c(from, to), set the span, and reversing them reverses the strip. With several facet panels, guides use the plot's light.

References

Karline Soetaert, plot3D, colkey colour keys.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = 1:4, y = 1:4)
d$z <- with(d, x + y)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, fill = z))
p + geom_surface_3d() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(guide = guide_colourbar_3d()) + coord_3d()
p + geom_surface_3d() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral",
    guide = guide_colourbar_3d(along = NULL, shading.range = TRUE)) +
  coord_3d(light = light_3d(mode = "lightness"))
p + geom_surface_3d() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_b(guide = guide_coloursteps_3d(shading.range = TRUE)) + coord_3d()
p + geom_col_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = factor(x))) +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = guide_legend_3d(shading.range = TRUE)) + coord_3d()
